items.question: What material blessings can arise from encountering the supreme person?
premises: A sonless person obtains sons.
A wealthless person obtains wealth.
items.inference: Encounter with the supreme person grants desired material gains.
items.plain_english: The sonless obtains sons, and the wealthless obtains wealth.

items.question: Which further benefits are bestowed upon one who beholds the supreme person?
premises: Life, fame, and glory are obtained.
Intelligence, wealth, knowledge, firmness, and cattle are obtained.
items.inference: Beholding the supreme person confers a wide range of worldly and personal benefits.
items.plain_english: One obtains life, fame, glory, intelligence, wealth, knowledge, firmness, and cattle.

items.question: How comprehensive are the enjoyments granted by seeing the supreme person?
premises: A person may desire various enjoyments.
Seeing the supreme person fulfills those desires.
items.inference: All desired enjoyments are obtained through the vision of the supreme person.
items.plain_english: Having seen that supreme person, one obtains whatever enjoyments one desires.

items.question: By what analogies is the supreme status of the sacred place established?
premises: The letter a is foremost among all letters.
The Gāyatrī is foremost among meters.
items.inference: These analogies illustrate a principle of supreme preeminence.
items.plain_english: As the letter a is foremost among all letters, and the Gāyatrī among meters,

rows.grounds: among all parts of the body

items.question: How does the analogy of the body reinforce the claim of supremacy?
premises: The head is the best among all limbs.
The goddess is addressed as witness to this comparison.
items.inference: The head’s supremacy among limbs parallels the supreme status being asserted.
items.plain_english: As the head is the best among all limbs, O great goddess,

rows.grounds: among those who restrain or govern

items.question: What divine hierarchies further illustrate the principle of preeminence?
premises: Varuṇa is foremost among aquatic beings.
Yama is foremost among restrainers.
items.inference: Divine rulers exemplify supremacy within their respective domains.
items.plain_english: As Varuṇa is foremost among aquatic beings, and Yama among restrainers,

items.question: Which natural exemplars complete the series of supreme comparisons?
premises: The milk ocean is best among oceans.
The lord of rivers is foremost among rivers.
items.inference: Natural domains also display a highest and most excellent member.
uncertainties: patiḥ of rivers may refer to the ocean as their lord
items.plain_english: As the milk ocean is best among oceans, and the lord among rivers,

items.question: What claim of uniqueness is made about the supreme person on earth?
premises: No equal to that person is seen on earth.
The statement is addressed to the goddess of gods.
items.inference: The supreme person is declared incomparable in the world.
items.plain_english: O goddess of gods, I see no one on earth who is equal to him.

items.question: How emphatically is the greatness of that sacred place affirmed?
premises: The word truth is repeated three times for emphasis.
That place is declared supreme and great.
items.inference: The sacred place is affirmed with utmost certainty as supremely great.
items.plain_english: Truth, truth, and again truth: that sacred place is supreme and great.

items.question: What heavenly enjoyments follow devotion at that supreme sacred place?
premises: One enjoys various pleasures.
Those pleasures are accompanied by divine women.
items.inference: Devotion at the sacred place leads to diverse heavenly enjoyments.
items.plain_english: Having enjoyed various and diverse pleasures accompanied by divine women,

items.question: What future births result from the merit gained at that sacred place?
premises: One may be born as a yogin among yogins.
One may be born as a householder who knows knowledge.
items.inference: Merit from the sacred place leads to auspicious future births.
uncertainties: jñānajño is an unusual compound; taken as knower of knowledge
items.plain_english: O goddess, one is born as a yogin among yogins, or as a householder who knows knowledge.

items.question: What ritual orientation is prescribed for viewing the southern ocean?
premises: One should face south.
One should behold the southern ocean.
items.inference: A specific bodily orientation is required for this sacred viewing.
items.plain_english: Facing south, one should behold the southern ocean.

rows.grounds: having saluted that; sandhi tat + namaskṛtya

items.question: What reward follows from bowing to the sacred Mandāra site?
premises: One bows to Mandāra.
Such homage leads to honor in Brahmā’s world.
items.inference: Reverence to Mandāra results in exaltation in Brahmā’s realm.
items.plain_english: Having bowed to Mandāra, Mandāra, one is honored in the world of Brahmā.

rows.grounds: merely by seeing; sandhi darśanāt + eva
let there be homage; sandhi namaḥ + astu

items.question: What salvific power is attributed to the mere sight of the mountain lord?
premises: The mountain lord is addressed as having Viṣṇu’s form.
Salutation is offered because sight alone is efficacious.
items.inference: Merely seeing the mountain lord confers a sacred benefit worthy of homage.
items.plain_english: O lord of mountains, whose form is Viṣṇu, by sight alone—salutation to you.

items.question: What liberation from rebirth follows from realizing knowledge of Brahman?
premises: One realizes knowledge of Brahman.
Such a person does not touch or see womb-residence.
items.inference: Realization of Brahman-knowledge prevents future rebirth in the womb.
items.plain_english: Having realized the knowledge of Brahman, he does not touch or experience residence in the womb.

items.question: What alternative periods of fasting are prescribed for the practitioner?
premises: Fasting may be observed for a year.
Alternatively, fasting may be observed for only a month.
items.inference: The practice allows different durations of fasting.
items.plain_english: Having fasted for a year, or else for only a month,

rows.grounds: in the northern part of Mandāra; sandhi mandārasya + uttare
a goddess or sacred presence named Yāmilā

items.question: Where is the blood-colored goddess Yāmilā located for worship?
premises: Yāmilā is located in the northern part of Mandāra.
She is described as blood-colored.
items.inference: The practitioner is directed to a specific location and form of Yāmilā.
uncertainties: yāmilā may be a local goddess name or epithet
items.plain_english: In the northern part of Mandāra is Yāmilā, blood-colored in appearance.

rows.grounds: with the kavaca mantra or armor
giver of dharma, wealth, and desire

items.question: What ritual means and benefits are associated with worshipping Yāmilā?
premises: She is to be worshipped with the kavaca.
She grants dharma, wealth, and desire.
items.inference: Worship of Yāmilā with the kavaca yields the three aims of life.
uncertainties: kavacena may refer to a protective mantra or ritual armor
items.plain_english: She is to be worshipped with the kavaca, for she grants dharma, wealth, and desire.

items.question: Which attendant goddesses are included in the prescribed worship sequence?
premises: Jayā and Vijayā are to be worshipped.
Bhadrakālī and Kapālinī are to be worshipped.
items.inference: The ritual includes worship of these four goddesses.
items.plain_english: One should worship Jayā and Vijayā, and also Bhadrakālī and Kapālinī.

items.question: Which central goddesses must be worshipped in the middle of the ritual?
premises: Bhavānī, Kālī, and Kālarātri are placed in the middle.
They are to be worshipped together.
items.inference: The central worship focuses on Bhavānī, Kālī, and Kālarātri.
items.plain_english: In the middle, one should worship Bhavānī, Kālī, and Kālarātri.

rows.grounds: by the vyāna breath or vital force

items.question: How is the practitioner instructed to perform the meditation being taught?
premises: Meditation is to be performed through meditation and vyāna.
The listener is asked to hear the teaching.
items.inference: The goddess introduces a specific meditative method involving vyāna.
uncertainties: vyānena may refer to a vital breath or a meditative technique
items.plain_english: One should perform the meditation through meditation and vyāna; hear my meditation, dear one.

items.question: What attributes of Kālarātri are invoked in this act of worship?
premises: Kālarātri has terrible, roaring laughter.
She removes hundreds of sins.
items.inference: Worship of Kālarātri invokes her fearsome power and sin-removing grace.
items.plain_english: I worship Kālarātri, with terrible roaring laughter, who removes hundreds of sins.

items.question: Which divine qualities are praised in the invocation of the goddess?
premises: The goddess is addressed as universal in form, auspicious, and pure.
She is addressed as odd-eyed and three-eyed.
items.inference: The invocation praises the goddess’s cosmic, pure, and powerful nature.
items.plain_english: O universal-formed, auspicious, pure one, O odd-eyed, three-eyed goddess.

items.question: What further epithets characterize the goddess in this concluding invocation?
premises: The goddess is called great night and wondrous-limbed.
She is called fond of secret dance and auspicious.
items.inference: The concluding invocation emphasizes the goddess’s mysterious and auspicious aspects.
items.plain_english: O great night, O wondrous-limbed one, O you who love the secret dance, O auspicious one.
